title: AI case summaries — the risk position before the first cohort

masthead.eyebrow: Risk context report · AI case summaries
masthead.headline: The model is only the final hop.
masthead.lede: The dangerous failure is not a wrong summary. It is a confident summary built from evidence the viewer is no longer authorized to see, with no record of what it was built from.

rows.text: Improve summary accuracy: tune the prompt, add citations, evaluate representative cases, ship behind a flag.
Treats the model as the whole system
Prove the evidence is still authorized at render time, not only at generation time.
Retrieval, caches, audit and fallback all cross the customer boundary

blocks.title: Decision-changing insight
blocks.text: Offline factuality scores cannot establish launch safety if the online request can assemble evidence the viewer no longer has permission to see.

sections.label: Findings
sections.title: Four material findings, each with evidence and a probe

items.title: AUTH-07 — revocation and derived-cache invalidation are separate paths
items.text: The permission consumer clears retrieval keys; the summary worker keeps its evidence bundle until TTL expiry. A user can lose access and still receive a generated claim derived from the revoked record for up to fifteen minutes.
items.evidence: Permission event trace, staging run 1842 — single tenant, no cross-region delay, 2 days old

items.title: TRACE-03 — the audit event stores the summary, not the evidence snapshot
items.text: summary_generated records case ID, model, and output hash but omits evidence IDs and the authorization version. During an incident, operators cannot distinguish a model error from an authorization race, or reproduce what the model saw.
items.evidence: Audit schema at commit 4c1b9e2 — the production sink transform was not inspected

items.title: EVAL-12 — citations can be present while the claim overstates the source
items.text: The current evaluator checks citation existence and lexical overlap, not whether uncertainty or chronology was preserved. A qualified agent note can become a definitive customer-facing diagnosis while still pointing at the correct record.
items.evidence: Summary evaluation rubric v3 — no uncertainty-preservation dimension, 3 weeks old

items.title: FALL-01 — the source-only fallback renders and is permission-correct
items.text: The containment path exists behind its own flag and returns the source timeline with no generated prose. What is not yet proven is that it survives a failure injected mid-request rather than before the request begins.
items.evidence: Fallback integration suite — passes today, but has no mid-request fault injection

blocks.text: Prioritized by worst-credible impact. Severity and likelihood are review assessments, not measured rates; each mitigation is routed to a named owner.

rows.text: Likely — async revocation against a 15-minute cache
Certain in any dispute or incident
Persist evidence IDs and the authorization snapshot in the audit event
Grade entailment, uncertainty, and chronology with disagreement review
Inject timeouts at retrieval, generation, citation assembly, and render
One-day shadow queue before promising a human-review control

sections.label: Risk paths
sections.title: Small gaps combine into customer-visible failures

blocks.text: Neither path below needs a model error. Each is built entirely from behaviour the system exhibits today.

items.title: Permission revoked
items.text: The permission consumer clears the retrieval keys it owns.

items.title: Evidence cache survives
items.text: The summary worker's bundle is untouched and stays valid until its TTL expires.

items.title: Summary states the claim
items.text: Generation runs against evidence the viewer may no longer see, and renders it as prose.

items.title: Audit lacks lineage
items.text: The recorded event names the model and the output, not the evidence set.

items.title: Incident cannot reconstruct
items.text: Nobody can prove afterwards whether this was a model error or an authorization race.

blocks.title: Prevent, detect, contain
blocks.text: Prevent by binding the authorization version and evidence IDs to every generated result. Detect by measuring entailment, permission races, fallback entry, and review backlog. Contain by disabling generated prose while keeping the source timeline available. Shipping one layer and deferring the others silently is the failure mode.

sections.label: Launch gate
sections.title: What must be true before the first cohort?

blocks.label: Controls that must show measured containment
blocks.ask: Which controls must be proven by measurement — not by design review — before any customer sees generated prose?

options.summary: Reject stale evidence and invalidate derived caches after revocation.
Persist the evidence and authorization snapshot behind every result.
Prove containment at every mid-request failure boundary.
Measure workload and severity latency before calling review a control.
Grade uncertainty preservation and chronology, not citation existence.

blocks.label: Exposure gate
blocks.ask: Choose the evidence threshold that controls customer exposure.

choices.summary: Permit a cohort only after the revocation and replay probes pass.
pros: No customer sees generated prose until we can prove we could withdraw it.
The two probes are cheap and already scoped.
cons: Exposure waits on probe results, so the first cohort slips by roughly two weeks.

choices.summary: Collect online evidence with no generated prose visible to customers.
pros: Real traffic and real evidence at zero customer risk.
cons: Internal reviewers are not the population whose reaction we need to measure.

choices.summary: Requires an explicit review SLA and a capacity proof.
pros: Genuine customer signal arrives soonest of the three.
cons: Human review must hold at volume, and we have no capacity proof that it does.

blocks.recommendation: Block on containment and lineage. Revocation is the one property we cannot add after the fact — if generated prose reaches a customer record and we cannot withdraw it, no later gate recovers that — and the two probes cost about two weeks against a risk that is otherwise permanent.

blocks.label: Constraint that changes this gate
blocks.ask: What customer, regulatory, or operating constraint changes the gate you just chose?
blocks.placeholder: e.g. a tenant contract that forbids any generated prose over their records

blocks.title: Decision rule
blocks.text: A launch blocker needs a named owner, a measurable pass signal, and a tested rollback. Do not downgrade a blocker to a nice-to-have in order to unblock exposure.
